{{Location map|Japan Mapplot|coordinates={{Coord|37.29|140.12}}|caption=Iwase Kokuzō Shrine|width=256}}

'''Iwase no Kuni no Miyatsuko''' (''iwase no kuni no miyatsuko'') was a {{ill|kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造}} who ruled '''{{ill|Iwase Province|cs|Provincie Iwase|de|Provinz Iwase|fa|ولایت ایواسه|ja|石背国|ko|이와세국|nl|Iwase (provincie)|pt|Província de Iwase|simple|Iwase Province|zh|石背國|zh_yue|石背國|qid=Q1166897}}''', said to have been located in {{ill|Iwase District|ja|石背郡}} (''iwase no kōri'') of {{ill|Mutsu Province|ja|陸奥国}} in the {{ill|ritsuryō system|ja|令制国|lt=ritsuryō provinces}}, corresponding to the present-day Iwase area of {{ill|Sukagawa, Fukushima|ar|سوكاغاوا (فوكوشيما)|azb|سوکاقاوا، فوکوشیما|ce|Сукагава|ceb|Sukagawa (lungsod sa Hapon)|cs|Sukagawa|de|Sukagawa|eo|Sukagawa|es|Sukagawa|fa|سوکاگاوا، فوکوشیما|fi|Sukagawa|fr|Sukagawa|gl|Sukagawa|id|Sukagawa, Fukushima|it|Sukagawa|ja|須賀川市|ko|스카가와시|mg|Sukagawa|mzn|سوکاگاوا، فوکوشیما|nl|Sukagawa|pl|Sukagawa|pt|Sukagawa|ro|Sukagawa|ru|Сукагава|sr|Сукагава|sv|Sukagawa|tg|Сукагава|tl|Sukagawa, Fukushima|tr|Sukagawa|tt|Сукагава|uk|Сукаґава|ur|سوکاکاوا، فوکوشیما|uz|Sukagava (Fukushima)|vi|Sukagawa, Fukushima|war|Sukagawa, Fukushima|zh|須賀川市|zh_classical|須賀川市|zh_min_nan|Sukagawa-chhī|zh_yue|須賀川|qid=Q819664|lt=Sukagawa City}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}.

== Overview ==
=== Ancestry ===
* According to the "Kokuzō Hongi" of the ''{{ill|Sendai Kuji Hongi|ja|先代旧事本紀}}'', during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seimu|ja|成務天皇|lt=Emperor Seimu}}, '''Takemiyorime-no-Mikoto''' (''takemiyorime no mikoto''), son of {{ill|Takekoro-no-Mikoto|ja|建許侶命}}, was appointed kuni no miyatsuko.

=== Clan ===
'''{{ill|Kimikobe clan|ja|吉弥侯部|lt=Kimikobe clan}}''' (''kimikobe-uji''; possibly no kabane). The ''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|cs|Nihon Sandai Džicuroku|de|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|es|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fa|نیهون ساندای جیتسوروکو|ff|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fr|Nihon sandai jitsuroku|it|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|ko|일본삼대실록|pt|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ru|Нихон сандай дзицуроку|simple|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|zh|日本三代實錄|zh_classical|日本三代實錄|qid=Q1052981}}'' records that in {{ill|Jōgan (Japan)|ja|貞観 (日本)|lt=Jōgan}} 5 ([[863]]), Kimikobe-no-Toyono was granted the surname '''Mutsu Iwase-no-Asomi'''.

== Tutelary Shrine, etc. ==
* Otakiya Shrine (''otakiya-jinja'') – Said to originate from a small shrine that Takemiyorime-no-Mikoto himself enshrined. It enshrines the ancestor Takekoro-no-Mikoto and Takemiyorime-no-Mikoto. The shrine's name derives from Takemiyorime-no-Mikoto cooking the new grain and offering it before the deity. It is enshrined in Shinmachi, Sukagawa City, north of the {{ill|Sukagawa Interchange|ja|須賀川インターチェンジ|qid=Q11664791}} on the {{ill|Tōhoku Expressway|ja|東北自動車道}}. The same-named shrine located at 45-1 Suwamachi, Sukagawa City, east of the {{ill|Tōhoku Main Line|ja|東北本線}}, is a new shrine after being transferred to Suwamachi, and also enshrines {{ill|Takeminakata-no-Mikoto|ja|建御名方命}}, invited by {{ill|Nikaidō Tameuji|ja|二階堂為氏}} from {{ill|Suwa Taisha|ja|諏訪大社}} in {{ill|Shinano Province|ja|信濃国}}.
* Iwase Kokuzō Shrine (''iwase kokuzō-jinja'') – Enshrines Takemiyorime-no-Mikoto, and descendants of the kuni no miyatsuko are said to have hereditarily held the priesthood<ref>Naganuma Town Board of Education, ''Naganuma-machi no Densetsu'', [http://www.db.fks.ed.jp/txt/10020.003/html/00095.html p.95]</ref>. Enshrined at 37 Naganuma-Toyomachi, Sukagawa City, Fukushima Prefecture.
* Shirakata Shrine – Said to have been invited from {{ill|Hiraoka Shrine|ja|枚岡神社}} in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国}} by Takemiyorime-no-Mikoto. Enshrined at 245 Aza-Machiuchi, Imaizumi, Sukagawa City, Fukushima Prefecture. The Yoshida family, descendants of the Iwase no Kuni no Miyatsuko, served as hereditary priests and transmit the "Iwase Kokuzō Keizu."
